title: JWTs: Promises and Betrayals
topic: JSON Web Tokens (JWT): how they work, what they actually guarantee, and the well-known ways they get attacked and misused — with defenses
summary: A threat-model tour of JSON Web Tokens: what a signature really promises, how alg:none, key confusion, and header injection subvert it, and the claim checks, lifetimes, and storage choices that hold the line.

concepts.title: Anatomy of a JWT — header, payload, signature, and what each part actually promises
Signed is not secret — JWS vs JWE, base64url is not encryption
The algorithm zoo — HS256 vs RS256/ES256, and the alg:none betrayal
Validation done right — exp, nbf, aud, iss, clock skew, and the checks libraries skip
Key confusion and header abuse — RS256-to-HS256 downgrade, kid and jku injection
The logout problem — revocation, token lifetimes, refresh tokens vs server sessions
Where tokens leak — localStorage, URLs, logs, referrers, and safer storage/transport
Cheatsheet — a JWT validation checklist and which claims to require, always

images.prompt: A strict International-Typographic-Style editorial illustration on a pure white background. Two simple flat geometric locks sit side by side, drawn as thin black outlines. A single flat key shape, solid vivid red, is drawn twice: once inserted into the left lock at a normal upright angle, and once inserted into the right lock rotated awkwardly, clearly the same key in a lock it was never cut for. The right lock's outline is also vivid red to mark it as compromised. Pure flat vector, no gradients, no shadows, no texture, no text or letters anywhere, generous white space, asymmetric composition weighted to the left. Palette strictly: white, black, one vivid red. Target size ~1280x720px, 16:9 landscape; compose with the subject centred and safe margins, since the art is letterboxed into a 16:9 box.
images.alt: A key labelled for one lock being used to open a different lock
images.caption: One key, two locks. The public key was never a secret — the mistake was building a door that would accept it as one.
